{{2020–21 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}}
The '''2020–21 Houston Cougars men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Houston]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cougars were led by seventh-year head coach [[Kelvin Sampson]] as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. It was the third season that the team played its home games at the [[Fertitta Center]].  They won their first ever [[2021 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] to clinch an auto-bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they were selected as a #2 seed in the Midwest Region.  The team advanced to the Final Four for the first time since [[1983–84 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|1984]]. They eventually lost to [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] in the Final Four who went on to become the national champions that season.

==Previous season==
Houston finished the 2019–20 regular season 23–8, 13–5 in [[2019–20 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]], finishing tied for first place and winning a share of the regular season title.  They entered as the No. 2 seed in the [[2020 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], which was ultimately cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].

==Schedule and results==

===COVID-19 impact===
{{main|Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports}}

Due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the Cougars' schedule was subject to change, including the cancellation or postponement of individual games, the cancellation of the entire season, or games played either with minimal fans or without fans in attendance and just essential personnel.

*The Cougars began a home-and-home series with LSU and Alabama beginning in the 2020–2021.<ref>{{cite tweet |last=Rothstein |first=Jon |user=JonRothstein |number=1252618014140370946 |date=21 Apr 2020 |title=Sources: Houston and LSU will begin a home-and-home series next season at the Fertitta Center. Return game in Baton Rouge in 21-22. |link=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/1252618014140370946 |access-date=21 Apr 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |user=JonRothstein |number=1314913578374164480 |date=10 Oct 2020 |title=Sources: The home-and-home series between Alabama and Houston remains on as scheduled starting this season in Tuscaloosa. Terrific game for both teams. }}</ref>  Both were eventually postponed due to the pandemic.
*Houston added a game vs. [[Our Lady of the Lake University|Our Lady of the Lake]] on February 6.<ref>{{cite news |title=UH adds basketball game against Our Lady of the Lake |newspaper=Houston Chronicle |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Houston-basketball-adds-game-Our-Lady-of-Lake-15922204.php|date=3 Feb 2021 |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph }}</ref>
*The game @ [[2020–21 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] originally scheduled for February 21 was moved to Houston.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cincinnati-Houston Men's Basketball Game Set for Feb. 21 Changes Location |url=http://theamerican.org/news/2021/2/10/cincinnati-houston-mens-basketball-game-set-for-feb-21-changes-location.aspx|date=10 Feb 2021}}</ref>
*Houston added a game vs. [[2020–21 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers men's basketball team|Western Kentucky]] on February 25.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hilltoppers Add Nationally Televised Road Game at No. 6/5 Houston on Thursday; FIU Series Altered |url=https://wkusports.com/news/2021/2/21/mens-basketball-hilltoppers-add-nationally-televised-road-game-at-6-5-houston-on-thursday.aspx|date=21 Feb 2021}}</ref>
*The game @ [[2020–21 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]] originally scheduled for March 7 was moved to Houston, after COVID-related issues with Memphis forced the first scheduled matchup between the teams scheduled for February 14 to be postponed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Announces Schedule Change|url=https://uhcougars.com/news/2021/2/26/mens-basketball-houston-announces-schedule-change.aspx|date=26 Feb 2021}}</ref>
